---
title: "Fixed Points and Stability of the Lorenz–63 System (Julia)"
format: html
jupyter: julia
---

## 1. Introduction

The **Lorenz–63 system** is a classic nonlinear dynamical system introduced by Edward Lorenz (1963) to model simplified atmospheric convection.  
It is defined by the following set of ordinary differential equations:

\[
\begin{cases}
\dot{x} = \sigma (y - x), \\
\dot{y} = x(\rho - z) - y, \\
\dot{z} = xy - \beta z.
\end{cases}
\]

Here, \( \sigma \), \( \rho \), and \( \beta \) are positive real parameters controlling the system’s dynamics.  
We shall use **Symbolics.jl** to derive the fixed points and analyse their linear stability.

---

## 2. Define the system and compute equilibria

```julia
using Symbolics

# Define variables and parameters
@variables x y z sigma rho beta

# Define the Lorenz-63 system
dx = sigma*(y - x)
dy = x*(rho - z) - y
dz = x*y - beta*z

# Solve for fixed points: dx = dy = dz = 0
fixed_points = solve([dx ~ 0, dy ~ 0, dz ~ 0], [x, y, z])

println("Fixed points of the Lorenz–63 system:")
for (i, fp) in enumerate(fixed_points)
    println("  Point $i: ", fp)
end
```

---

## 3. Compute the Jacobian matrix

```julia
# Define the vector field
f = [dx, dy, dz]
vars = [x, y, z]

# Jacobian matrix
J = Symbolics.jacobian(f, vars)

println("Jacobian matrix J(x, y, z):")
display(J)
```

---

## 4. Evaluate the Jacobian at each fixed point

```julia
for (i, fp) in enumerate(fixed_points)
    # Substitute the fixed point into the Jacobian
    subs_dict = Dict([k => v for (k,v) in zip(vars, fp)])
    J_fp = substitute.(J, Ref(subs_dict))
    
    # Compute eigenvalues symbolically
    eigs = Symbolics.eigenvalues(J_fp)
    
    println("\n=== Fixed point $i ===")
    println("Coordinates: ", fp)
    println("Jacobian:")
    display(J_fp)
    println("Eigenvalues:")
    display(eigs)
end
```

---

## 5. Discussion

At the **origin** \((0,0,0)\), the Jacobian is

\[
J_0 =
\begin{pmatrix}
 -\sigma & \sigma & 0 \\
 \rho & -1 & 0 \\
 0 & 0 & -\beta
\end{pmatrix},
\]

whose eigenvalues are

\[
\lambda_1 = -\beta, \\
\lambda_{2,3} = \frac{1}{2}\left[-(\sigma + 1) \pm \sqrt{(\sigma - 1)^2 + 4\sigma\rho}\right].
\]

This fixed point is **stable** when \( \rho < 1 \) and becomes **unstable** for \( \rho > 1 \).

The other two equilibria (symmetric about the origin) appear only when \( \rho > 1 \); they are stable for intermediate parameter values and lose stability through a Hopf bifurcation as \( \rho \) increases.

---

## 6. Conclusion

This example demonstrates how **Symbolics.jl** can be used to:
- Symbolically derive fixed points of nonlinear systems,
- Compute Jacobians,
- Analyse local stability through eigenvalues.
